{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABaiJuEg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEIqYA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 71, "title": "Preserve SCSP level-7 interrupt rearming during MC68EC000 execution", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `3144c937efa742c734dd35dd9a23bd601360b34e`, `Sound::advance_cpu_cycle` samples `Scsp::interrupt_level()` only when starting a new architectural boundary (`src/sound/transactions.rs:198–202`). Pending operations replay an earlier CPU snapshot; completion replaces the live CPU with that replayed execution. SCSP events continue while an instruction is pending, but their interrupt-level transitions are not delivered to the sound CPU.

The standalone core already detects transitions into level 7 (`src/m68k.rs:187–190`). The integrated scheduler can nevertheless miss this valid sequence: the first level-7 interrupt is acknowledged; its handler begins a long instruction with SR.I=7 while the SCSP request remains asserted; the SH-2 clears the acknowledged source, leaves the output low, then reasserts level 7 during that instruction and holds the new request until acknowledgement. Both instruction-boundary samples see 7, so the second edge is lost and level comparison cannot recover it at mask 7. This conclusion follows from source inspection; a runtime reproduction has not been executed during planning.

The existing division interrupt regression holds a level-3 request until delivery. It does not cover this rearm sequence. Lost sound interrupts affect guest synchronization independently of arithmetic correctness or successful audio demos.

## Expected outcome

SCSP interrupt-output changes reach retained MC68EC000 input state during in-flight computation and bus waits. Replay preserves that state and consumes an accepted request once. Architectural interrupt entry still waits for the appropriate instruction boundary.

The hardware contract is [Motorola MC68000 User’s Manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/MC68000UM.pdf), §3.5 and §6.3.2, printed pp.3-6 and 6-12–6-13: requests must remain asserted until acknowledgement; transitions from a lower level to 7 generate nonmaskable requests; held level 7 can also qualify through level comparison after software lowers the mask. Do not base mandatory results on requests withdrawn before acknowledgement.

[Sega SCSP User’s Manual §4.2, interrupt control](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/scsp/hon/p04_2c.htm), Figures 4.55–4.58, defines the SCSP route, manual pending bit, enables, clearing and programmed interrupt levels. Reconcile the corresponding ST-077-R2 interrupt-register sections and applicable corrections before implementation. Document any evidence-backed correction to this task with exact primary references.

Keep this increment focused on interrupt-input propagation and replay/reset lifetime. General prefetch completion, data-dependent division timing and unrelated synthesis changes remain separate work.

## Context and reproduction

Use the existing sound transaction scheduler, SCSP interrupt registers and original 68k reset/retirement fixtures.

Construct the reproducer without injecting CPU interrupt state:

1. Execute an original sound program and deliver its first SCSP level-7 request through real MMIO and autovector handling.
2. Keep SR.I=7 and enter a long handler instruction while the first SCSP source remains asserted.
3. After the first CPU acknowledgement, have the SH-2 clear that source, maintain a low interval comfortably longer than the modeled input synchronization interval, then reassert it before the long instruction completes. Keep the second request asserted until its acknowledgement.
4. Require completion of the interrupted computation followed by a second level-7 handler entry. Record actual completed register writes and CPU boundaries to prove the transitions occurred inside one instruction.

Expected event order and handler records must be authored from the documented contract before production changes. Separate architectural requirements from unmeasured synchronization/equal-edge conventions; avoid ambiguous electrical pulse widths.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a failing native integrated regression for the valid rearm sequence above. Demonstrate that inherited production behavior misses the second interrupt, rather than merely failing compilation or fixture setup.
- [ ] Implement retained interrupt-input propagation across long internal computation, pending memory operations and replay completion. Cover SCSP pending, enable and level-register changes plus scheduled device events that change the output. Do not repeat completed MMIO or introduce an unbounded interrupt queue.
- [ ] Add independent native vectors for rearming at SR.I=7, a continuously held 7 without a new transition, an ordinary initial lower-to-7 assertion, and held-7 recognition after software lowers SR.I. Preserve held maskable interrupt delivery and SCSP main/sound acknowledgement independence.
- [ ] Assert completed computation, saved PC/SR, autovector, handler counts, separately scheduled IACK/stack accesses and absence of premature entry. Exercise pending bus work and verify that replay neither loses a retained transition nor manufactures duplicate acceptance.
- [ ] Verify CPU reset cancellation through SNDOFF/SNDON and cold reset. Preserve existing SCSP reset, RESET-output, trace-entry and instruction-retirement regressions. Compare event/handler records across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 with passive inspection enabled and disabled.
- [ ] Supply or extend an original MIT-licensed SH-2/68k fixture with reproducible source, bytes and hashes. The SH-2 must generate the SCSP transitions through production MMIO; the 68k must compute and publish its own handler records. Run identical bytes natively and through production Wasm in the required headless browser suite under `/saturn-rust/`.
- [ ] Include distinguishing guest controls: omit the intervening clear, omit the second assertion, and change a computation operand. Assert independently authored results, repeat cold boots, and prove the new guest oracle rejects inherited behavior. Host code may observe records but must not supply handler results or directly set CPU IRQ state.
- [ ] Update architecture, conformance and validation records with exact primary references, implementation/test links, actual results and remaining deviations. Correct stale claims relevant to this increment without marking broader rows complete.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native/Wasm warnings-denied Clippy, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and complete `npm run test:browser`. Preserve existing tests and Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, WebAudio, input, backup and local-file/privacy regressions.

This is partial progress toward #17. Remaining CPU/peripheral, bus/cache/reset/arbitration, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain mandatory. Genuine BIOS execution and broad commercial-game compatibility remain unverified. Leave the umbrella scope open; administrative closure or green CI does not establish hardware completion.

## Optional validation

Additional mixed SCSP-source stress using the same original fixtures. No personal firmware, commercial media, physical console, human approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
